question.problem:
On a certain afternoon, the total number of people $N(t)$ visiting the city's zoo is given by the function

$$
N(t)=30+4{\int }_{0}^{t}(10-2x)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time (in hours) since noon.  

At what time is the number of people in the zoo at a maximum, and how many people are at the zoo at that time?

The maximum number of people is
{{field-1}}
after
{{field-2}}
hours.
question.worked_solution:
To find when the number of people at the zoo is at maximum, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(30+4{\int }_{0}^{t}(10-2x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(30)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{\int }_{0}^{t}(10-2x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(10-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4(10-2t)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=0$:

$$
4(10-2t)=0\,⟹\,t=5
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=5.$ To find out how many people are in the zoo when $t=5,$ we figure out $N(5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(5) & =30+4{\int }_{0}^{5}(10-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =30+4{[10x-{x}^{2}]|}_{0}^{5} \\  & =30+4[(10\cdot 5-{5}^{2})-(0)] \\  & =30+4\cdot 25 \\  & =130\end{aligned}
$$

Since $30<130$, we conclude that the maximum number of people at the zoo is $130$, and this will happen after $5$ hours.
